correctness.rationale: Condition on all previously revealed individual rankings and assigned schools; exactly k_t=n-t+1 choices remain and r_t previously assigned schools are held by lower-priority students. Uniformly random fresh ranking makes justified envy probability r_t/(k_t+r_t), independent of the entire history, and iterated conditional expectation proves all student indicators independent. Adjacent inversion parameters give exact zero-envy and both-envy differences by rational algebra. If the both-envy probability can rise, r>=1 and s>k-1+r force n>=5. The five-student witness changes the two-claimant tail 4/15 to 3/10, verified independently by exact defining-rule enumeration. The checker tested all 33 priority orders for n<=4, all 43 admissible priority corrections, and two five-student witness orders. Enumerations are supplementary to the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The new finding establishes the all-position exact joint distribution of students experiencing justified envy, strict monotonicity of a completely envy-free outcome under adjacent priority correction, and the sharp first five-student failure of full tail monotonicity. Searches of published mathematical records, and relevant primary full-text theorem/appendix sections, found no statement implying those conclusions. Hamdan (2026) covers expected blocking triples/Kemeny optimization; earlier random-priority analyses cover means or inclusion, not the joint fixed-priority count. Residual risk: an equivalent statement could occur in unindexed school-choice or probabilistic permutation literature.
residual_risks: Conditional-independence observation or equivalent adjacent-inversion tail paradox may have appeared in unindexed or inaccessible literature.
No comprehensive systematic search of every adjacent branch of matching-economics literature is possible; publication priority remains independently unverified.
The common-school-priority and independent-uniform-preference assumptions are narrow and must not be dropped in downstream use.

value.rationale: The natural count of distinct students with justified envy is a distributional fairness risk that expected blocking pairs do not determine. The joint independence law gives exact probability calculations for any fixed order. More significantly, a sharp five-student counterexample shows that improving a priority inconsistency raises the probability of a wholly fair outcome while making multiple concurrent fairness complaints more likely; four students never suffice. This is a structural frontier with direct use in assessing upper-tail risk, not an arbitrary table cell or a routine change of notation.
